 This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of MV Act, praying to modify the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1695/2014 dated 14.12.2018 by the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT No.VI, at Vijayapura and allow this appeal and enhance the compensation as claimed in the claim petition, in the interest of justice and equity.

These appeals coming on for admission,
through physical hearing/video conference, this day T.G.Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
JUDGMENT

In these appeals, the appellants have challenged the common judgment dated 14.12.2018 passed in M.V.C.No.1981/2014 and M.V.C.No.1695/2014 respectively on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.VI, Vijaypur (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal' for short).
2.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.VI, Vijaypur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Briefly stated, the facts are that, the petitioners in M.V.C.No.1695/2014 were the wife and children of one Namadev Chalekar, the deceased.
The petitioner in M.V.C.No.1981/2014 is one Shankar, the injured.

The injured as well as the deceased met with an accident near Kazi Garage in Mangalweda, while the injured was riding the motor cycle bearing No.MH- 13/W-9914, which was hit by a Truck bearing No.HR- 55/N-1928.
The deceased was the pillion rider of the motor cycle.
The injured suffered compound fracture of left Tibia and Fibula and the deceased succumbed to injuries.
4. The wife and children of the deceased sought compensation of Rs.50 lakhs and the injured sought compensation of Rs.10 lakhs before the Tribunal.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.2,44,980/- to the dependants of the deceased and Rs.4,93,200/- for the injured with 9% interest.

5. The petitioners have pleaded inadequacy in the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the ground that the income was taken at Rs.5000/- for the deceased and Rs.6,000/- for the injured,
that there was no addition of future prospects, the disability assessed for the injured was on the lower side and they have sought for re-assessment and enhancement of compensation.
6.

According to the learned counsel for petitioners, the deceased as well as the injured were earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing agriculture as well as business, but the Tribunal did not consider it.
The Tribunal has not properly assessed the compensation towards pain and suffering, loss of amenities, loss of income during laid-up period and also loss of income due to disability.

It is also contended that the Tribunal did not consider the income of the deceased properly, even though a sum of Rs.7,500/- is being considered in the Lok Adalat and under conventional heads also,

3

entities.text: Janabai And Ors vs Amarjeet Singh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: inadequate compensation is awarded.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for Insurance Company contended that the amount granted towards conventional heads is on the higher side, that the deceased was aged 70 years, there is no question of considering future prospects, the income taken is on par with the prevailing minimum wages,
having regard to the medical evidence, the disability of the injured was considered in excess though the limb disability was assessed at 40% and there is no need for enhancement and supported the impugned judgment.
8.
We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.

9. We find from the impugned judgment that there is no dispute as to the accident, cause of the accident, injuries sustained by the injured, death of the deceased on account of the injuries suffered in the accident and entitlement of the petitioners to claim compensation.

It is pertinent to note that the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/- and income of the injured at Rs.6,000/-, but in a case of this nature, uniformity is paramount and therefore, the income assessed by the Tribunal is not proper and it is not in consonance with the income that was prevailing in the year 2014 when the accident occurred.

Hence, the income ought to have been taken at Rs.7,500/-
for both the injured as well as the deceased, as there is no proof of income for both of them.

10. The petitioners/legal heirs of deceased claim that the deceased was aged 58 years, but Ex.P4/Postmortem report points out that the deceased was aged 70 years and the Tribunal has rightly accepted it.

By applying the principles laid down in National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others - 2017 ACJ 680, for the age of 70 years, there is no scope for addition of future prospects, but the future prospects for the age between 40 to 50 years shall be 25%, as the injured was aged 45 years.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others - 2017 ACJ 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Award of compensation towards conventional heads has been settled in the above judgment.

For the age of 70 years, the applicable multiplier as per decision of Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121, is '5' and for the age of 45, it is '14'.
11.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation (2009)6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The medical records point out that the injured spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment, which the Tribunal has properly considered.
PW- 3/Dr.Shekhar Prakash Malve is the Doctor, who has assessed the disability of the injured at 40% of the limb and the Tribunal has taken 15% disability.

The injured has suffered compound fracture of Tibia and Fibula of his left lower limb and assessment of disability at 15% is proper and we do not find any force in the submission of the counsel for the petitioner that whole body disability shall be taken at 40%.

12. Ex.P7/medical certificate and Ex.P8/discharge card shows that the petitioner was hospitalized for a period of 45 days for which he has to be adequately compensated towards attendant, food and conveyance charges which the Tribunal has considered on the lower side.

13. If all these factors are taken into consideration, the assessment of compensation on account of death of Namadev is: notional income of Rs.7,500/- per month, the dependants consist of three Janabai And Ors vs Amarjeet Singh And Anr on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186172707/
4 members, hence, 1/3rd has to be deducted, i.e., Rs.7,500/- - 1/3rd = Rs.5,000/- x 12 x 5 =
Rs.3,00,000/-.

entities.text: Janabai And Ors vs Amarjeet Singh And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under conventional heads, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded as loss of consortium to the first petitioner only, as two sons are major, towards loss of estate Rs.15,000/- and towards funeral expenses, Rs.15,000/- is considered.

Thus, the total compensation works out at Rs.3,70,000/- as against Rs.2,44,980/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.1,25,020/- which is rounded off to Rs.1,25,000/-, it is just and adequate compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.
14. As regards the compensation to the injured is concerned, towards pain and suffering, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is assessed; medical expenses of Rs.3,00,000/- is maintained as assessed by the Tribunal.
The petitioner having sustained fracture of both bones of left leg, he shall be laid up for minimum of six months.

Hence, towards loss of income during laid-up period will be Rs.45,000/-
(Rs.7,500/-x6); towards loss of amenities and discomfort, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is assessed and towards attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is assessed.

15. As regards loss of income due to disability is concerned, the petitioner was earning Rs.7,500/-
and if 25% of future prospects is added, it comes to Rs.7,500/- + Rs.1,875/- = Rs.9,375/- x 12 x '14'
multiplier x 15% whole body disability comes to Rs.2,36,250/-.

16. Thus, in all, the petitioner/injured is entitled to Rs.6,91,250/- as against Rs.4,93,200/- awarded by the Tribunal, thereby there is enhancement of Rs.1,98,050/- rounded off to Rs.1,98,000/-, which is just compensation to which the petitioner is entitled in the facts and circumstances of the case.

17. Accordingly, the appeals filed by the petitioners deserve to be allowed by enhancing the compensation as referred supra.
18.

In the result, we pass the following;
ORDER Both the appeals are allowed in part.

The judgment and award dated 14.12.2018 passed in M.V.C.No.1981/2014 and M.V.C.No.1695/2014 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.VI,
Vijaypur, is hereby modified.
